title: Coefficient change commutes with inverse image and extension by zero
statement:
Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a map of commutative condensed rings and write
$K_{\Lambda'}=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}K$ ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]).

1. For a morphism $f\colon X\to Y$ and $K\in\D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ there is a
   natural isomorphism $(f^*K)_{\Lambda'}\simeq f^*(K_{\Lambda'})$ in
   $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda')$. For $g\colon Y\to W$ the isomorphism for $g\circ f$ is
   the composite of those for $f$ and $g$ under $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$.
2. In the standing separated finite-type scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], for a locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ (in particular an open
   immersion $j$ or a closed immersion $i$) and $M\in\D(S_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ there
   is a natural isomorphism $(a_!M)_{\Lambda'}\simeq a_!(M_{\Lambda'})$, compatible with
   composition of immersions; for $a=i$ closed this reads
   $(i_*M)_{\Lambda'}\simeq i_*(M_{\Lambda'})$.
Here $a_!$ is the exact locally closed extension by zero, applied termwise to unbounded complexes; its factorization-independent meaning and composition identifications are those of [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence]. All tensors are ordinary derived tensors, without completion.

3. For a composite $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$ one has
   $(K_{\Lambda'})_{\Lambda''}\simeq K_{\Lambda''}$, compatibly with the isomorphisms in (1) and (2).

proof.text:
Write $A_Z=\Lambda_Z$, $B_Z=\Lambda'_Z$, $T_Z=B_Z\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_Z}-$, and $r_Z=\operatorname{Res}_{A_Z\to B_Z}$. The internal module objects are the ordinary module sheaves over the coefficient ring sheaf: [det-def-sfb-module-objects-sheaves] describes an action $A_Z\otimes M\to M$, and the tensor universal property identifies it with the bilinear sheaf action $A_Z\times M\to M$; the unit, associativity and linearity equations are exactly the module-sheaf equations. The relative tensor products agree by their balanced coequalizer universal property. We use this identification, retaining the coefficient ring sheaf rather than replacing it by a constant-ring coefficient category. For every scheme map $h:Z\to W$, [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] identifies $h^{-1}A_W=A_Z$ and $h^{-1}B_W=B_Z$ without an admissibility assumption on the condensed rings. The square in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change] identifies the pulled-back ring map with $A_Z\to B_Z$. Thus [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies module pullback over both rings with exact inverse image. Restriction of scalars changes only the action, by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], so $r_Zh_B^*=h_A^*r_W$ canonically, already on complexes. Applying inverse image to the coequalizer defining $B_W\otimes_{A_W}P$ gives
$$h_B^*(B_W\otimes_{A_W}P)\cong B_Z\otimes_{A_Z}h_A^*P.$$
Indeed inverse image is a left adjoint, hence preserves that coequalizer, and its tensor comparison is invertible by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-tensor]. The displayed identification is $B_Z$-linear: the action is on the first tensor factor on both sides.

source.place: (1), coefficient identifications and the ordinary tensor calculation

proof.text:
Choose a K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The pullback $h_A^*P$ is again K-flat with flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat]. By [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], $B_W\otimes_{A_W}P$ computes $T_WK$ and $B_Z\otimes_{A_Z}h_A^*P$ computes $T_Zh_A^*K$. Exactness of $h_B^*$ lets us apply it to the first representative without resolving again. The inverse of the termwise isomorphism in step 1 therefore defines
$$\theta_h:T_Zh_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_B^*T_W$$
in the derived category of $B_Z$-modules. It is natural because the tensor map is natural before localization and derived scalar extension is computed on K-flat resolutions. The coefficient identifications respect composition by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. For $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to W$, the termwise map obtained directly for $gf$ and the map obtained successively for $g,f$ both send the class of $b\otimes (gf)^{-1}p$ to the same class with the $B_X$ action on $b$. Equivalently both are the maps of the same pulled-back coequalizer induced by the identical maps on $B_W\otimes P$. Its universal property proves their equality. Hence $\theta_{gf}=(f_B^*\theta_g)\circ(\theta_f g_A^*)$ under the canonical inverse-image composition maps, proving (1).

source.place: (1), K-flat realization and the composition equation; Stacks 0G7E and 0D6D

proof.text: For clause (2), the schemes of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] are Noetherian: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applies. Every open in each affine chart is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so the complementary opens used below are quasi-compact morphisms. For complementary $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to $A_X$ and $B_X$. It supplies exact $j_!,i_*$, $j^*j_!=1$, $i^*i_*=1$, the two cross-vanishings, and the sheaf short exact sequence. Exact inverse images and exact extension functors descend termwise to all unbounded complexes by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]; the ordinary adjunctions descend as well, since both functors are exact. In particular $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*$ hold unboundedly. The pair $(j^*,i^*)$ detects isomorphisms there: for any derived morphism take all cohomology maps, use [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to commute the exact restrictions with cohomology, apply the sheaf short exact sequence to the kernels and cokernels, and then use [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. No bounded-below recollement theorem is being extended by assumption.

source.place: (2), standing-scheme scope and exact open/closed functors; Stacks 09BM, 09AH, 09AA, 09BN

proof.text:
For $j$ open, both $T_Xj_{!,A}$ and $j_{!,B}T_U$ are left adjoint to the same functor $r_Uj_B^*=j_A^*r_X$. In detail, for $N\in D(X,B)$ the adjunctions give natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(T_Xj_{!,A}M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,j_A^*r_XN)=\operatorname{Hom}(M,r_Uj_B^*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_{!,B}T_UM,N).$$
Here the scalar adjunction is the one in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change], the exact open adjunction is [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] derived as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and the middle equality is the action equality proved in step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] these define the canonical unit-compatible isomorphism $\beta_j:T_Xj_{!,A}\cong j_{!,B}T_U$. This is exactly the isomorphism $T^X\circ D(j_!)\cong D(j_!)\circ T^U$ of [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso]: that definition is the conjugate, along the same adjunctions $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$ and $T\dashv D(\operatorname{Res})$, of the canonical comparison $D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_U})D(j^*)\cong D(j^*)D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$ of [def-sfb-derived-comap-upper-star-iso], which is termwise the action identification of step 1 (both are the identity on underlying sheaves after the coefficient isomorphisms $\alpha_j,\alpha'_j$) used in the middle equality, so the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] identifies the two. Its restriction to $U$ is $\theta_j^{-1}$ after $j^*j_!=1$: taking adjuncts reduces this assertion to the identity transformation of $r_Uj_B^*$, because $j^*$ applied to the open unit and counit is the identity. This also verifies naturality in $M$ in the category with the new coefficient action. No flatness of $A_X\to B_X$ was used.

source.place: (2), the alternative proof by equality of right adjoints

proof.text:
For $i$ closed put $H=T_Xi_{*,A}M$ and define an actual $B_X$-linear derived morphism
$$\beta_i:H\xrightarrow{\eta_i}i_{*,B}i_B^*H\xrightarrow{i_{*,B}(\theta_i^{-1})}i_{*,B}T_Zi_A^*i_{*,A}M\xrightarrow{i_{*,B}T_Z(\varepsilon_i)}i_{*,B}T_ZM.$$
The unit and counit here come from the exact adjunctions of step 3. By the triangle identity, $i_B^*\beta_i$ is $\theta_i^{-1}$ after the closed counit identifications, so is invertible. Moreover $j_B^*H\cong T_Uj_A^*i_{*,A}M=0$ by step 2 and the cross-vanishing in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], and $j_B^*i_{*,B}T_ZM=0$. Detection from step 3 proves $\beta_i$ is invertible. All three arrows are natural transformations in $B$-module derived categories; this proves the new coefficient linearity before passing to an underlying $A$-module comparison. The construction is the closed projection-formula unit specialized to the coefficient algebra.

source.place: (2), closed immersion case, expanding the unit construction of the projection formula

proof.text:
For a locally closed $a=v\circ c$, $c$ closed and $v$ open, use [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] and define
$$\beta_a:T_Xv_{!,A}c_{*,A}\xrightarrow{\beta_v}v_{!,B}T_Vc_{*,A}\xrightarrow{v_{!,B}\beta_c}v_{!,B}c_{*,B}T_S.$$
It is natural and invertible by steps 4 and 5. Under $a^*a_!=1$, its restriction is $\theta_a^{-1}$: the two restrictions are $\theta_v^{-1}$ and $\theta_c^{-1}$, whose composite is $\theta_a^{-1}$ by step 2. The cited coherence lemma supplies factorization identifications, the identification with $i_*u_!$ when $a=i\circ u$, and full faithfulness: between objects in the essential image of $a_!$, restriction $a^*$ is faithful. To compare two factorizations, identify their extension functors by the cited canonical comparisons in each coefficient category. The source $T_Xa_{!,A}M$ is isomorphic to $a_{!,B}T_SM$ by the displayed composite for either factorization, so both source and target lie in the essential image of the same $a_{!,B}$. Both restricted maps are $\theta_a^{-1}$; faithfulness therefore makes the two maps equal. For $b:T\hookrightarrow S$, compare $\beta_{ab}$ with $(a_{!,B}\beta_b)\circ(\beta_a b_{!,A})$, using the canonical composition identifications of that lemma. Both maps have source and target in the essential image of $(ab)_{!,B}$ (use the displayed isomorphisms), and restriction to $T$ gives $\theta_{ab}^{-1}$ in both cases by step 2. Faithfulness proves the required equality, including mixed open/closed compositions. This proves all of (2).

source.place: (2), locally closed factorization, independence and composition

proof.text:
For $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$, restriction of scalars is transitive already on module complexes: composing the two actions gives the action along the composite ring map, by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] and functoriality in [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. Hence $T_{\Lambda',\Lambda''}^XT_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}^X$ and $T_{\Lambda,\Lambda''}^X$ are left adjoint to the same restriction functor, by the derived scalar adjunction. The unit-compatible isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives $\tau_X:(K_{\Lambda'})_{\Lambda''}\cong K_{\Lambda''}$. This is the usual tensor reassociation, with the final coefficient action retained: if $P$ is a K-flat representative with flat terms, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] applied to the identity underlying topos and $A_X\to B_X$ makes $B_X\otimes_{A_X}P$ K-flat over $B_X$. Thus both functors are computed without another resolution and $\tau_X$ is
$$C_X\otimes_{B_X}(B_X\otimes_{A_X}P)\longrightarrow C_X\otimes_{A_X}P,\qquad c\otimes(b\otimes p)\longmapsto cb\otimes p,$$
where $C_X=\Lambda''_X$, with inverse $c\otimes p\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes p)$. The balancing relations give the two inverse equations; each map is $C_X$-linear. Its normalization agrees with the scalar units $p\mapsto1\otimes p$, which identifies this chain isomorphism with the adjunction-defined $\tau_X$.

source.place: (3), associativity of derived extension, with the coefficient action and nonflat case explicit

proof.text:
For inverse image, compare the two composites from $T_{\Lambda',\Lambda''}^XT_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}^Xf_\Lambda^*K$ to $f_{\Lambda''}^*T_{\Lambda,\Lambda''}^YK$ using $\tau$ and the two $\theta$ maps. On the K-flat representatives from steps 2 and 7, both maps send $c\otimes(b\otimes f^{-1}p)$ to the class of $cb\otimes f^{-1}p$. Since these are the same maps on the defining balanced tensor coequalizers, they agree, and localization preserves this equality. For an open $j$, the two coefficient-extension comparisons are conjugate to the identical equality of right adjoints $r_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}r_{\Lambda',\Lambda''}j^*=r_{\Lambda,\Lambda''}j^*$, and their units agree by the normalization in step 7; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] proves equality. For closed $i$, apply $i^*$ to the two routes, using the closed counit: they become the inverse-image equality just proved. Both sources and targets belong to the essential image of $i_{*,\Lambda''}$ by step 5, so faithfulness of restriction from [lem-sfb-locally-closed-extension-coherence] proves equality before restriction. For any locally closed $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, the required equality, with $T_{AB}$, $T_{BC}$, $T_{AC}$ denoting the three scalar extensions, is explicitly
$$a_{!,C}(\tau_SM)\circ\beta_a^{BC}(T_{AB}^SM)\circ T_{BC}^X(\beta_a^{AB}M)=\beta_a^{AC}M\circ\tau_X(a_{!,A}M).$$
Both routes start at $T_{BC}^XT_{AB}^Xa_{!,A}M$ and end at $a_{!,C}T_{AC}^SM$. Step 6 identifies the source with $a_{!,C}T_{BC}^ST_{AB}^SM$, so both objects lie in the image of $a_{!,C}$. Apply $a_C^*$ and the identifications $a_C^*a_{!,C}=1$: each restricted beta is the inverse theta by step 6, and the equality becomes precisely the inverse-image/tower equality proved at the start of this step, evaluated at $a_{!,A}M$ and then restricted via $a_A^*a_{!,A}M=M$. The Hom bijection in the cited coherence lemma gives the displayed equality before restriction. This proves both compatibility squares in (3).

source.place: (3), the two compatibility squares with inverse image and extension by zero
